grid.chosen: 1x (115 BPM); 0.5x matched 97.5 % vs 97.1 % but halves every cut point — kept 1x, verify kick parity after render

splice.why: owner 2026-10-13: ~90 s so viewers can follow each step; best chroma/MFCC match among 14–20-bar gaps (16 bars)

demo.label: in-game product demo (second clip, 60-90 s): real BC screens operated, Thai captions, light music bed, no voice-over. Separate edit; the keys above stay the trailer's record.
demo.source: analysis/source-stay-with-me.mp3 (Mixkit 'Stay With Me', 127.504 s) — same track as the trailer. It is the only music bed on disk; nothing was downloaded.
demo.out: public/audio/bgm-demo.wav (48 kHz PCM_16 stereo, 77.4147 s, 14.9 MB)

grid.note: identical to the trailer's grid — same source, bar-aligned splice, so video beat n is at t0 + n*T continuously. A new timeline module can reuse SOURCE_BEAT0 / BEAT_INT verbatim.

splice.why: tools/splice2.py over gaps 21-27 (the only gaps that land 70-85 s: length = 127.504 - gap*2.08702). 0.9907 is the best score at >=75 s and matches the trailer's own accepted 0.9914; same cut point as the trailer (bar 30), shorter tail, so the two clips share the song's opening and its ending.

rejected.why: highest score, but 71 s leaves no reading room; the whole gap-27 family (0.9976/0.9972/0.9971) is the project's old 70 s edit
longest in range, lowest score, and it drops the song's opening bars (the only low-density passage)

video.srcBeat_of_videoBeat: n for n <= 120, n + 96 for n >= 120
video.why_total: beat 145.5; the 100 ms RMS falls below -70 dB at 76.167 s = f2285, and the bed runs to 77.415 s (2322 f) so the file never hard-cuts (same rule as the trailer's 2790 vs 94.11 s)

level.why: the trailer's 0.4 (-8 dB) over Thai captions that must be read would compete; -12.4 dB puts the bed ~4.4 dB under the trailer. The track has no quiet section to hide in (per-bar RMS is -15 dB +/-1.5 across all 59 bars), so level, not section, is what makes it read differently.

notes: Peak of the written wav is 0.00 dBFS with 2135 samples at full scale — inherited from the source mp3 (decoded peak +1.06 dBFS at 74.5 s); the trailer's bgm-edit.wav has the same 2702. The crossfade window itself peaks -0.14 dBFS. At bgm 0.24 it is 12 dB down and inaudible; do not re-gain the source.

Drum drops (quiet bars, good for a caption to be read against): video beats 32 (f509, kick 0.30) and 64 (f1010, kick 0.84). Loud bars to avoid putting a caption's first frame on: video beats 12 (f196), 96-100 (f1510-1573), 136 (f2137, the final hit).
Output audio offset 42.3 ms (AAC priming) is unchanged — same encoder. Re-verify with tools/backtest2.py after the first render.
